# Command line

FLUX Simulation Engine: runs a FLUX bundle deterministically against the FLUID contract it references, and packs the evidence.

```bash
# start with a small working project
fluxsim init demo
cd demo
fluxsim run . --verify --ship -o out

# look up what an error code means
fluxsim explain FLX-3105
```

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`fluxsim init`](./init.md) | write a small working project into a new directory |
| [`fluxsim validate`](./validate.md) | validate a FLUX bundle |
| [`fluxsim plan`](./plan.md) | execute the loop once and record plan.json |
| [`fluxsim apply`](./apply.md) | apply a recorded plan and write its run directory |
| [`fluxsim run`](./run.md) | plan + apply, with --verify/--ship sugar |
| [`fluxsim verify`](./verify.md) | golden regression + row conformance + RFC-04 + fidelity |
| [`fluxsim ship`](./ship.md) | the fidelity gate, then the evidence pack |
| [`fluxsim replay`](./replay.md) | re-execute a recorded plan; assert its digest |
| [`fluxsim calibrate`](./calibrate.md) | declared-scorecard calibration for a Playback |
| [`fluxsim accuracy`](./accuracy.md) | outcome-accuracy gate: register, score, record |
| [`fluxsim gate`](./gate.md) | RFC-04 enforcement gate: decide, conform |
| [`fluxsim expr`](./expr.md) | flux-expr/1: evaluate an expression, print an attribute model |
| [`fluxsim describe`](./describe.md) | self-describe this installation |
| [`fluxsim plugins`](./plugins.md) | list installed vertical packs |
| [`fluxsim explain`](./explain.md) | print the catalog entry for one FLX-nnnn code, or list them all |

## Options every command accepts

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--version` | print the version and exit |
| `-j, --json` | emit machine-readable JSON |

`--json` and `-j` may come before or after the command.

## The JSON envelope

With `--json` every command prints one document of the same shape, so a caller never has to guess which command produced it or read stderr for the reason it failed:

```json
{
  "stage": "validate",
  "exitCode": 0,
  "ok": true,
  "artifacts": {},
  "error": null
}
```

`artifacts` is the command's own output. `error` is `null` on success, otherwise `{"code": "FLX-nnnn", "message": "..."}`, where `code` is `null` for a failure with no catalogued code. A usage error is an envelope too, with `exitCode` 2.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | The command ran and succeeded. |
| `1` | The command ran and failed. The message says why; a catalogued failure carries an `FLX-nnnn` code. |
| `2` | A usage error: the command line itself was wrong, so nothing ran. |
| `3` | `fluxsim gate decide` only: the request was decided, and the policy said no. |

## Environment

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `FLUX_ZONE` | The run's declared zone for sovereignty checks, used when `--zone` is not given. |
| `FLUX_DEBUG` | Any non-empty value prints the traceback of an unexpected failure. |
| `FLUX_NO_PROGRESS` | Any non-empty value silences the progress lines and the `next:` hints that a terminal otherwise gets on stderr. |
